newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ROBSON, VALDANO STRUGGLE TO PUT TOGETHER TEAMS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROBSON, VALDANO STRUGGLE TO PUT TOGETHER TEAMS.

text.p: Valencia coach Jorge Valdano and his Barcelona opposite number Bobby Robson will be forced to cobble together sides from squads decimated by injuries and international duty for Sunday's Spanish league clash.

Both men will be going all out for victory. Robson cannot afford any more setbacks if he is to close the nine-point gap on leaders Real Madrid, while Valencia badly need a result to maintain their challenge for a UEFA Cup place.

Valdano's men had the better of the game between the two sides earlier this season but the coaches were reduced to mere extras as Brazilian striker Ronaldo scored an extraordinary hat-trick in Barcelona's 3-2 victory.
The two coaches had met before -- but in very differenct circumstances.
Valdano was part of the Argentine squad that knocked Robson's England side out of the 1986 World Cup in a game made infamous by Diego Maradona's 'hand of God' goal.
Valdano subsequently traded in his place in the Real Madrid midfield for the hot seat on the bench at Tenerife and then at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium itself.

But the elegant Argentine lost his way at Real after winning the league in his first year in charge and has ended up with a Valencia side that is still reeling from losing striker Predrag Mijatovic to Real.
The comings and goings of Brazilians Romario and Viola, together with some well-publicised dressing-room and boardroom conflicts have left Valdano with a tough job on his hands.
To make matters worse, Valencia are scraping the bottom of the barrel to find players ahead of the big match with Barcelona.
Newly-signed Argentine Ariel Ortega will miss the game through international duty, as will Croatian striker Goran Vlaovic and Russian midfielder Valery Karpin.
Three other players are injured and influential defender Enrique Romero is suspended.
Gabriel Moya is struggling to get fit, as is fellow striker Jose Galvez who was taken ill when flying back from Monday's game at Sporting Gijon.
The 2-1 defeat in Gijon led to rumours that Valdano had been handed an ultimatum to win this weekend's game.
But he dismissed it as "a journalistic invention".
Robson is himself no stranger to such inventions.
The former England coach recently hit out at a reporter who suggested that the Barcelona players had decided for themselves on a key substitution in a cup match with Atletico Madrid.
But Robson would no doubt appreciate some advice in picking a team for the Valencia game.

Gheorghe Popescu will be playing for Romania, while a question mark hangs over the fitness of the three Portuguese players -- goalkeeper Vitor Baia, winger Luis Figo and defender Fernando Couto -- who will fly in from the World Cup qualifier in Belfast the previous evening.
Baia's uncertainty contributed to the defeat at Real Sociedad the last time he tried to juggle national and club commitments.

Utility player Luis Enrique Martinez is out suspended, while a broken arm in Wednesday's Cup win at Las Palmas means that overlapping full back Sergi Barjuan will join reserve striker Angel Cuellar and international defender Abelardo Fernandez on the injury list.
Robson's last doubt is partly of his own making.

His clashes with Giovanni, who has recently been dropped in favour of Ivan de la Pena, have led the Brazilian midfielder to ask for a transfer. Robson is now only likely to pick Giovanni if he is really needed.
However, Barcelona have one of the world's strongest squads and are likely to leave at least one international on the bench, even in the current circumstances.
"The squads are there for that," said Robson's number two, Jose Mourinho.
Valdano might hope that his own club could have built a squad to do the same for him.
